panel.appCSSHint:
CSS for the app itself — its colours and its own layout.
Tokens set on :root reach articles too.

The app's colours are CUSTOM PROPERTIES, so restyle by changing a value rather
than every rule that reads it:

  --bg           page and sheet background   --fg          all text
  --bg-card      cards, fields, buttons      --fg-soft     DISABLED states
  --bg-bar       the search bar              --fg-faint    (and the ⌕ mark)
  --accent       highlights, pressed states  --line        borders
  --accent-soft  the accent's tint           --line-soft   hairlines
  --link         result headwords            --focus       focus rings
  --paper-bg     the reader's paper          --paper-bk-image  its texture
  --label / --label-quiet   what labels, headings, hints and counts read;
                            both are the ink unless something says otherwise
                            (the "Quiet labels" preset points them at the greys)
  --wd-article-bg / --wd-article-fg   the article surface inside a frame

html[data-dark] is true whenever the page is dark, "auto" included;
html[data-theme="dark"] is true only when the reader pinned dark by hand.
panel.articleCSSHint:
CSS for what dictionaries render, in every article.
Use :host, :root > body to reach the article's own root.

An article is a frame of its own, and the app's custom properties reach it, so
the same names work here:

  --wd-article-bg   the article surface      --wd-article-fg   its text
  --fg, --fg-soft, --fg-faint   the app's text: --fg is all of it, the two
                                greys are the DISABLED states
  --link, --accent              headwords and highlights
  --bg-card, --line             surfaces and borders

Selectors land INSIDE the article: p, a, table, div, body — and :host when the
dictionary is drawn as a shadow root. Nothing here reaches the chrome; that is
what the App box is for.

system.messagesHint: The notes this app puts on screen while it is starting and while it is looking a word up — the “Starting…” line, the waiting art, the “N of M ready” counter, and the “Looking up …” line in the floating window. They are true and they pass in a moment, which is why they can be turned off: with this off, a window stays empty until its results arrive. A failure is still reported, and so is the note that the answers below are for a different form of the word you typed.
system.accessHint: Other apps on this phone can reach the dictionary server. With this on, they can look words up but cannot change anything — no importing, indexing or removing dictionaries, and no settings. Turn it off if another app should be able to change things too. Takes effect the next time the app starts.
